newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Keidanren calls for ODA reforms.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Keidanren calls for ODA reforms.

text.p: The Japan Federation of Economic Organisations (Keidanren) is planning to come up with a proposal to reform the country's Official Development Assistance (ODA) programme, a Keidanren official said on Wednesday.

Keidanren's ideas include a plan to reorganise ODA-related domestic organisations, such as the Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund, the Japan International Cooperation Agency and various sections of the ministries related to the official ODA programme, into a single government agency.
"The idea of combining the organisations is only one part of our wide range of proposals. We're not focusing only on this idea," the official of the powerful business lobby said.
The ODA budget will likely be reduced in the future, and Keidanren said it saw a need to review the programme to cut out any inefficiencies.
"We'll give our opinion to the government from the private sector's point of view," the official said, adding "nothing formal has been decided at this point".
Keidanren plans to announce its proposals on April 15 at a meeting of its board of directors.
